title: The Book of Poetry
attributionNote: The odes gathered folk and court songs, dynastic hymns and sacrificial verses over several centuries; the collection was fixed at three hundred and five pieces by the Han.
description: Legge's 1876 translation of the Shih Ching, the first complete English rendering of the classic with the Chinese text and his commentary: the airs of the states, the odes of the royal domain and the sacrificial hymns, with the introduction that traces the collection's formation and the notes that explain each ode's occasion.
historicalContext: Legge's separate translation of the Book of Poetry appeared between his editions of the Four Books and the Sacred Books of the East volumes and carries the fuller scholarly apparatus of the two. It prints the odes with the Chinese text facing the English.
availabilityNote: Complete as the volume prints it: the odes of the four parts, streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one printed ode per chapter. The volume's preface and its introduction are not part of the work; Legge's notes and the Chinese text stand on the pages themselves and are kept, because they are part of the printed page the reader sees.
